candidate.title: NS-seq
candidate.scope: Schematic-level nascent strand sequencing (NS-seq), specifically the λ-exonuclease enrichment route drawn in the assigned NS-seq row: replication-associated DNA → λ-exo digestion → purification → amplification → DNA. The introductory nascent-DNA cartoon is an explanatory repeat of the origin context, not a parallel preparation branch. The neighboring Repli Seq and smMIP rows and clipped labels from other rows are outside scope. The matching catalogue page is headed NS-Seq: Nascent Strand Sequencing and reproduces the same operation captions. Foulk et al. (2015) identifies the RNA-primer protection mechanism, the actual isolated-DNA substrate and the sequencing-library interface; its unshown control preparations and buffer comparisons are not additional target workflows. NS-Seq and NS-seq here are capitalization variants of the same name, not distinct methods.

states.label: Replication-associated DNA entering λ-exo enrichment
features: Diagram: black parental DNA and blue nascent DNA in an origin/chromatin cartoon; strand-end chemistry is not explicitly labeled.

Paper-supported chemical substrate: isolated replicative-intermediate DNA enriched before digestion and made single-stranded and phosphorylated; the matching catalogue specifies 5′ phosphorylation. This preparation history is upstream of the drawn route and is not a drawn operation.
Nascent strands bear protective 5′ RNA primers. The sequenced target is DNA associated with replication initiation, not an RNA-expression measurement.

states.label: Amplified DNA representing the selected fragments
features: Terminal schematic product is three blue DNA lines labeled DNA; adapters, indexes and sequencing reads are not drawn.

DNA sequence is the readout carrier. The corresponding primary implementation converts selected single-stranded fragments to double-stranded DNA before preparing an Illumina library; the diagram does not resolve that interface into individual operations.

Sequencing these products can localize enriched genomic regions used to infer replication origins, with λ-exo sequence/structure bias. Enrichment alone neither proves an active origin nor directly establishes a folded G4 in vivo.

operations.label: Lambda 5′ to 3′ exodeoxyribonuclease (λ-exo); Digestion
operations.description: λ-exo acts on the DNA substrate and depletes susceptible parental DNA, leaving a population enriched for protected nascent DNA. The drawing places an enzyme icon at the origin-derived DNA and fades background material in the digestion panel. This is selective digestion of isolated DNA in the cited implementation; chromatin/protein icons explain biological origin rather than specify an in situ reaction.
operations.mechanism: 5′-to-3′ DNA exonuclease digestion is impeded by the 5′ RNA primer of nascent strands. λ-exo is an added catalytic reagent, not another workflow branch. GC-rich DNA and G4 structures can also impede digestion, so protection is not uniquely nascent-strand-specific.
operations.information_effect: Enrichment couples survival of a physical DNA fragment to its resistance to λ-exo; surviving fragments carry genomic sequence information. This enriches replication-associated sequences while retaining digestion-dependent background.

operations.label: Amplify
operations.description: Copy the purified DNA population to produce the multiple DNA molecules drawn at the terminal DNA label. The caption does not specify an amplification enzyme or resolve sequencing-library preparation into its internal steps.
operations.mechanism: Amplification is depicted without specified chemistry. At the associated paper’s library interface, recovered single-stranded DNA is made double-stranded with random hexamers and Klenow before fragmentation and Illumina library construction. This clarifies the strand-conversion interface without adding unshown operation nodes or claiming that Amplify alone is a complete library recipe.
operations.information_effect: DNA copies retain the genomic sequence identity of selected fragments for sequencing-based localization of enrichment. Copying does not distinguish RNA-protected nascent strands from GC-rich or G4-protected survivors.

method_scopes.rationale: All three operations belong to the single NS-seq row, whose explicit λ-exo, Digestion, Purify, Amplify and DNA captions match the NS-Seq catalogue schematic. Foulk et al. describes the same λ-exo-based nascent-strand enrichment and its library interface. This establishes schematic applicability, not identical complete implementations across the broader NS-seq family. BrdU-based examples, LexoG0 control libraries, plasmid tests and buffer alternatives discussed in the sources do not create additional target methods or depicted branches.

checks.rationale: The correction retains the visible origins/G4 caption and generic DNA endpoint, then explicitly limits their interpretation using the primary paper. GC-rich and G4-protected parental sequences can survive alongside RNA-protected nascent strands. Thus survival alone neither identifies every fragment as origin-derived nor measures folded G4s in vivo. This is a justified interpretation of the bias evidence, not an assertion that the diagram depicts a G4-specific readout. The paper identifies LexoG0 as a control, and the candidate correctly keeps that unshown control outside the graph.
